summary: The Pentagon's All-domain Anomaly Resolution Office (AARO) released its FY2025 UAP report this week, months past the statutory deadline, documenting 319 new cases and expanded satellite analysis capabilities. Meanwhile, federal officials outlined formal pathways for UAP whistleblowers to come forward, addressing a long-standing barrier to disclosure. Luis Elizondo, the former Pentagon UAP official, addressed persistent claims he's managing a "controlled narrative," while journalist Ross Coulthart noted Elizondo remains constrained by security oaths that limit what he can publicly discuss. A mysterious UAP event near Virginia's coast drew Navy attention and Pentagon investigation, adding another data point to the growing catalog of incidents. These developments suggest momentum building on the bureaucratic side of disclosure, even as questions persist about what information remains classified and why.
